card_policy.comment: # 卡号形状(task_id_pattern, AIPOS-F252): 受控发布 / finalize / lybra-deploy 的归属解析只读它, 产品无内置默认; show 给出按现有卡号前缀推出的建议值(仅建议), 值经 Owner 确认后先预演再 --confirm(写治理根 card_policy.json 并落账)

legacy.meta: # project.json 说明键({keys})同样经产品写入口更新(人肉期旧文免手改), 先预演再 --confirm
legacy.meta_none: # project.json 说明键写入口 lybra project set-meta: 待 config.schema project_json 声明这些键后可用(未声明 = 拒 META_KEY_UNDECLARED)
legacy.t1: 落点声明: project.json paths 经产品写入口声明(免手改)
legacy.c1_head: # 键名与取值按 config.schema project_json.paths 校验(未知键拒 / finalize_mode 枚举); 先 --dry-run 看 diff, 再 --confirm
legacy.c1_stage: # 阶段档案(阶段快照)不在缺省位置时同样声明: --key {key} --value <相对治理根路径>(未声明 = 缺省落点; 落点下无快照 = finalize 阶段闸门拒)
legacy.p1: 为什么先做: 后两步都按声明落点工作——冻结按 queue_root 找卡, 收编按 return_root 写报告骨架、loop 按声明找产物; 落点未声明时取缺省值, 人肉期项目的真实落点未必是缺省, 骨架会落错位置。人肉期项目的 Return/裁决/队列/授权落点逐项声明(可多对 --key/--value; 与缺省相同也显式声明: 收编要求 config.schema project_json.paths.adoption.required_declared_keys 已显式声明, 否则拒 ADOPT_PATHS_UNDECLARED)。阶段档案(阶段快照)若不在缺省位置, 一并声明 {key}(相对治理根): Lybra 内部 finalize 的阶段闸门按此落点核阶段快照, 未声明而缺省位置无快照 = 拒(AIPOS-F145)。预演首行标明目标项目与 project.json 绝对路径, 核对无误再 --confirm; 在目标项目治理根下运行可省项目名(目标 = 该根 project.json#project, 解析不出即拒, 绝不回落 home 级活动项目; 显式项目名与所在治理根不一致 = 拒)
legacy.t2: 存量冻结: 人肉期已结束/不再推进的卡一次声明为历史(迁移基线)
legacy.c2_head: # 先 --dry-run 核对将冻结的卡与各卡 lint 问题计数, 无误后改 --confirm(清单只追加; 解冻 = --unfreeze)
legacy.p2: 为什么在收编之前: 收编认冻结(冻结卡拒 ADOPT_LEGACY_FROZEN), 先把不再推进的卡一次声明为历史, 仍在途、要继续推进的卡用 --exclude 留出(交给下一步收编); 冻结卡不被 state lint 报 ERROR、不被 next 当待推进, 门拒对其写动作
legacy.t3: 在途卡收编: 门补铸 claim 记录、绑定既有分支、建卡工作树
legacy.c3_head: # 每张在途卡: 先预览(零写入, 含授权判定与全部拒因), 无拒因后改 --confirm; 收编后与新卡同样只用 lybra loop 推进
legacy.p3: 为什么最后: 收编写报告骨架与 claim 记录, 依赖前两步(落点已声明、历史卡已冻结)。--branch = 该卡产物所在的既有分支(卡 lane.repo 仓内); 卡分支名与之不同时卡分支建在其 tip 上。拒因(声明 transitions nodes.N1.adoption.guards + config.schema project_json.paths.adoption.guards)一次列全: 卡面意图必填缺项 / 分支不存在 / 已有门生 claim / 已冻结 / 落点未声明 / 卡分支分叉 / 建树失败 / 授权不覆盖。已有手写 Return 不被覆盖: loop 按交回判据要求补 commit_sha / tree_hash / branch, 拒因原文给出补法

check.role_invalid: role 文件格式错误; 重跑工位接入步(Step {audit_step} / {exec_step})
check.no_policy_ref: role 文件缺 owner_policy_ref; 核对 Step {grant_step} 项目授权是否覆盖本工位实例(主机段)后重跑 lybra sync

cred.source_active: the Owner-credential holder in the gate registry: {holder} (declared active project {declared})
cred.source_single: the only Owner-credential holder in the gate registry: {holder}
cred.why_many: the home root {home} has {count} connection.json files holding an Owner credential ({holders}) and no declared active project to choose by
cred.why_none: none of the gate registry sources of the home root {home} (the home root itself and each existing project's .lybra/connection.json) holds an Owner credential (the gate has never run with this home root: lybra serve start; or the Owner credential lives elsewhere)
cred.reason: {why}. Regenerate this guide with --owner-connection-json <the connection.json the gate serve reads that holds the Owner credential> (or replace {conn} / {ws} in the step 3 / 4 commands with it and its workspace)

ws.source_default: config.schema default project_json.paths.{key}.default_user_home ({template}; a project can declare it with lybra project set-paths)
ws.inside: Workstation root {absolute} ({source}) lies inside {label} {inner}: workstation directories hold workstation credentials and must stay out of the governance repo. Use --workspace-dir / --auditor-dir to give directories outside the governance repo, or change the declaration with lybra project set-paths {project} --key {key} --value <absolute path outside the governance repo>
ws.same_dir: {label} and {other} are the same directory {path}: one directory can be enrolled for only one instance (otherwise the first one's charter landing breaks). Give each workstation its own directory and rerun the guide (--workspace-dir / --auditor-dir)

grant.existing_error: The project's existing authorization cannot be read ({error}): check with lybra project grant show {pq} --home-root {hq} before deciding whether to sign
grant.existing_live: This project already has a project authorization: {rows}. No need to sign again in this step (sign would issue a new revision with this run's scope as the whole scope); when lanes / task modes / drivers / hosts fall short, add them with lybra project grant extend {pq} --home-root {hq} … (preview first); see the current state with lybra project grant show {pq} --home-root {hq}
grant.existing_envelopes: This project still has {count} legacy envelope(s) ({ids}; still honored, no longer issued): consider merging them into a project authorization: lybra project grant draft {pq} --home-root {hq} --from-envelopes (preview; the Owner adds --confirm to sign), or sign a new authorization with this step's commands

card_policy.title: Card ID pattern (card-policy task_id_pattern)
card_policy.purpose: Card ownership resolution for controlled release / finalize / lybra-deploy reads only this; the product has no built-in default
card_policy.when: Before the first card (already part of step 11); change it when the card ID rule changes

test_contract.title: Post-merge regression contract (set-test-contract)
test_contract.purpose: Time limit and execution mode of the full regression; lybra regression baseline records the main-side baseline from it, so most cards need not rerun the full main suite themselves
test_contract.when: When the product repo has a full test list and you want card-branch and main baselines to be reusable

release_target.title: Production release target (release-target)
release_target.purpose: Declare the production host + allowlist + release root; afterwards a card's production release goes only through lybra release plan → apply → verify (roll back with release rollback); bare ssh/scp/rsync is forbidden
release_target.when: When the project deploys to production (--owner-ref can be omitted when the authorization's hosts include the target host)

pi_model.title: pi model (set-model)
pi_model.purpose: Which model the pi executor / auditor launched by loop uses (must be a model configured in this machine's pi; check with pi --list-models)
pi_model.when: When you do not want pi's own default model (can be declared per role with --role executor / auditor)

headline.title: Board advisor card (project headline)
headline.purpose: The advisor's summary card on the board home page: title / in progress / recently done
headline.when: After onboarding, and whenever the project phase changes

gate.same_host: ; same machine = loopback per same_host_rule, port taken from that source

harness.not_declared: --advisor-harness {kind} is not a declared advisor session harness; valid values {allowed} (distribution.schema harness_semantics.kinds.<kind>.advisor_session)
harness.host_forbidden: --advisor-host does not apply to --advisor-harness {kind} (declared harness_host=forbidden: that session runs on the governance-root machine and skills are delivered to the local session directory); for an advisor session on another machine use an --advisor-harness value with harness_host=optional
harness.host_blank: --advisor-host {host} contains whitespace (host names may not contain whitespace)
harness.host_required: Sessions of --advisor-harness {kind} may run on another machine: give --advisor-host <session machine> (or --host-segment); the advisor instance host segment does not default to the governance-root machine
harness.dir_required: The --advisor-harness {kind} session is on another machine ({host}): give --advisor-dir <absolute session directory on that machine> (a remote directory is recorded as given, never guessed)

mode.station_refused: --executor-mode {asked}: onboarding always follows the execution division (AIPOS-F256 / F262): code cards = sub-agent executor (--executor-mode {exec_mode}), non-code cards = pi executor workstation ({asked} mode), audits = pi auditor workstation, and the guide enrolls all three; the old flow where one pi executor workstation does everything is no longer generated. Rerun without --executor-mode

landing.git: The governance root must be inside a governance repo (git): lybra home git-init --home-root <home root> (one-time, no remote configured); the Owner configures origin and makes the first push per its output, then rerun this command
landing.push: Committed but not pushed: handle the reason in the output (no origin = the Owner configures a remote; remote conflict = follow the exit in the output), then rerun the same command
landing.staged: The governance repo has files staged by someone else, which this command leaves alone; ask their owner to commit or unstage them, then rerun

step1.not_git: # Governance repo not ready: home root {home} is not inside any git repo, so landing this step and every later card will fail closed. Initialize it once first (local git init, no remote, no push); the Owner configures origin and makes the first push per its output:
step1.landing: # Landing: commit and push exactly this step's products to the governance repo (AIPOS-F94; only the paths below, other changes in the governance repo untouched)
step1.title: Create the project (governance root under the home root + project.json + first stage snapshot) and land it
step1.purpose: Create the governance root {gov} of {project} under home root {home} (source: {home_source}): queue / records / governance docs / project.json, and write the first stage snapshot "project created" via governance add stage. The gate discovers projects only by scanning the home root; to put it elsewhere you can only change the home root itself (--home-root > LYBRA_HOME_ROOT > ~/.lybra/config.json home_root > default ~/.lybra/projects); governance roots outside the home root are never registered
step1.check: The output has 'Created project root:' and 'stage snapshot:' lines; verify: lybra project list --home-root <home root> shows the project name; the landing output has Verdict: PASS and '✓ Pushed to remote'
step1.fail_exists: The project root already exists and is not empty; confirm with lybra project list, then skip to Step 2
step1.fail_empty: The project name cannot be empty; rerun this step with a non-empty name
step1.fail_home: The home root is resolved only by the precedence ladder (see purpose); rerun this step with another --home-root
step1.creates_git: ; {home} becomes the governance repo (git, origin to be configured by the Owner)

step2.preview: # Preview first (prints the project.json diff to be written and the validation result, zero writes) for the Owner, then --confirm to write
step2.confirm: # --confirm writes and then commits and pushes project.json automatically (output 'landing: verdict=PASS …'), no separate governance-commit needed; if landing fails (exit 3) run the backfill command it prints once
step2.title: Declare the product repos (project.json repos / code_repo) and land them
step2.purpose: Write the product repo list into project.json (repos {default, items} + code_repo alias), validated against config.schema project_json.repos; a card's lane.repo names a repo, and worktree creation / finalize resolve through it. From then on each card is landed automatically when lybra loop closes it; commands that write governance truth (the project family / project grant / migrate) land automatically after --confirm; other non-card changes (hand-edited governance docs etc.) use governance-commit --paths
step2.check: --dry-run outputs 'project set-repos <project>: …' + one line per repo + the project.json diff (zero writes); --confirm outputs the written line and 'verdict=PASS committed=True pushed=True' (AIPOS-F159: landed right after writing); more than one repo requires --default
step2.fail_conflict: Paths must be absolute and default must be one of the repo names; fix the arguments and rerun (the preview already reports it; project.json unchanged)
step2.fail_not_established: Step 1 not done; run Step 1 first

step3.intro: # Preview first (zero writes: prints the full authorization revision and validation) for the Owner, then --confirm to issue it through the gate and land it; one authorization covers all lanes / task modes / drivers / hosts of the project, no more per-card or per-instance envelopes
step3.title: [Owner action ①] Sign the project standing grant {auth} (one grant for the whole project, replacing per-instance envelopes)
step3.purpose: With the Owner credential in the gate's central credential store ({conn}; source: {source}) the Owner signs the project standing grant {auth} through the gate's owner_decision_record: lanes {lanes} × task modes {modes} (an audit card is judged by the card it audits) × drivers {drivers}; hosts {hosts} (the host segments of the instance names this guide enrolls); launch {launch} (authorizes lybra loop to launch pi at the workstations automatically; the Owner removing --launch-harness = manual /go only); hard bounds: total cards + expiry. Grant before enrollment: the workstation enrollment pre-check needs an active grant covering it (otherwise refused, no code issued / no credential changed); afterwards lybra loop finds this grant by itself, no more per-card envelopes
step3.check: The preview outputs 'lybra project grant sign … verdict=PASS' and the full authorization revision; --confirm outputs 'signed {auth}' and 'wrote …/{auth}/r<revision>.md' (the gate-written record is authoritative); then lybra project grant show {pq} --home-root {hq} lists the grant with state active
step3.fail_scope: Signing a grant needs the Owner credential (owner_confirm); point --connection-json at the gate's central credential store
step3.fail_ambiguous: The command already carries --project {pq} (the gate's explicit target project); if PROJECT_AMBIGUOUS still appears, check that --project is a project registered under the home root and matches the project name argument
step3.fail_no_file: --connection-json must point at the connection.json the gate serve reads that holds the Owner credential; when it cannot be derived, regenerate this guide with --owner-connection-json
step3.fail_gate: The gate is not running or the address is unreachable: lybra serve status; this is a gate-side fault, report it to the Owner
step3.fail_refused: Fix the arguments per the refusals listed by the preview (lanes must be the step 2 repo names, task modes must be in range), then rerun the preview; the preview writes nothing
step3.creates: {gov}/<authorizations_root>/{auth}/r<revision>.md + owner_decisions record (landed into the governance repo)

step4.intro_local: # Preview first (shows the role / instance / governance root / validity and enrollment landing to be signed, no code issued, zero writes) for the Owner, then --confirm: issue the code + enroll in one go, the enrollment code stays inside this process (never printed, stored or put in argv). The credential lands in the governance root .lybra/ (loop takes the driver credential by governance root); the advisor kit (skills / charter) is delivered to the session directory: {landings}
step4.title_local: [Owner action ②] Issue a code and enroll the advisor into the governance root (enroll-deliver, the code never leaves the process) + deliver the advisor kit to the {label} session directory
step4.purpose_local: With the Owner credential in the gate's central credential store ({conn}) the Owner issues and redeems the advisor code for {project} on the governance-root machine in one command: the code embeds gate address {gate} (source: {gate_source}) and the governance root and is passed to enroll only inside this process (never printed, stored or put in argv); the redeemed advisor credential (projects=[{project}]) lands in {gov}/.lybra/ (connection.json + role, owner_policy_ref derived from the step {grant_step} project grant {auth}); per the distribution declaration ({dists}, harness={kind}) the product delivers the advisor kit through the same distribution engine to {landings} (the charter = rendering of the advisor charter master, including the keep-moving rules)
step4.check_local: --dry-run outputs 'roles enroll-deliver advisor: …' preview (no code issued, zero writes); --confirm outputs the executed line, the enrollment code_id and fingerprint (never the code itself) and '{kind} … → …' lines
step4.note_local: Advisor session directory {dir} ({dir_source}; default = the governance root; when another advisor on this machine already holds the governance root = the declared sub-path inside it; an explicit --advisor-dir wins; two advisors on one machine cannot share a session directory): every command in this guide names the governance root explicitly and does not depend on cwd; after the kit is delivered, restart the {label} session in the session directory to load it
step4.why_pull: the advisor kit declared for {kind} ({undelivered}) needs a local session directory; the session is at {session_at} = nothing lands on this machine (the charter / skills are pulled at session start, see Step 5; sync lists the rest as undelivered)
step4.why_none: no advisor kit is declared for {kind} = no distribution step
step4.intro_remote: # Preview, then --confirm (on the governance-root machine; issue + enroll in one go, the enrollment code stays inside this process): credential and identity land in the governance root .lybra/, and role records harness={kind} and where the session runs (--harness-host / --harness-dir) as given; {why}
step4.title_remote: [Owner action ②] Issue a code and enroll the advisor into the governance root (enroll-deliver, the code never leaves the process; {label} session, its location recorded as given)
step4.purpose_remote: With the Owner credential in the gate's central credential store ({conn}) the Owner issues and redeems the advisor code for {project} on the governance-root machine in one command (the code embeds gate address {gate}, source: {gate_source}; it stays inside this process): the advisor credential of the advisor ({label} session at {session_at}) lands in {gov}/.lybra/ (connection.json + role); role records harness {{kind: {kind}, dir: {dir}, host: {host}}} (a remote directory is recorded as given, not checked locally); no .pi wiring; {why}
step4.check_remote: --dry-run outputs a preview (no code issued, zero writes); --confirm outputs the executed line and 'harness …' recorded in .lybra/role; no .pi/ under the governance root, no advisor kit added on this machine
step4.note_remote: The advisor session ({label}) and the governance root may be on different machines: product commands run on the governance-root machine (a remote session goes through ssh); every command in this guide names the governance root explicitly and does not depend on cwd; {ssh}
step4.ssh_entry: when run over ssh, write lybra as the absolute entry path on the governance-root machine {cli} (a non-login ssh does not put ~/.local/bin on PATH)
step4.fail_envelope: The step {grant_step} project grant is not signed or does not cover this instance (driver / host); check lybra project grant show {pq} --home-root {hq} (pre-check refusal = no code issued, no credential changed)
step4.fail_unknown_root: The gate or this machine cannot find the project under the home root (step 1 not done, or the gate uses another home root); make sure the gate and step 1 use the same home root
step4.fail_no_role_cred: --connection-json must point at the central credential store holding the Owner credential (the connection.json the gate serve reads)
step4.fail_harness: Fix the --harness value to one of the valid values listed in the output and rerun (pre-check refusal, no code issued)
step4.fail_dir_key: must be an existing absolute directory
step4.fail_dir: For a session on another machine add --harness-host <session machine> (a remote directory is recorded as given, not checked locally); on the same machine create the directory first
step4.fail_delivery: The credential is already in place; rerun lybra sync --harness-root <governance root> (do not rerun the enrollment)
step4.fail_rollback: When enrollment fails the gate has already revoked the code (output shows it was rolled back); if the rollback failed, revoke by hand per the exit in the output and rerun this step

step5.precheck: # Prerequisite self-check (read-only): project / product repos / project grant / advisor credential all present
step5.steady: # Advisor kit steady-state check: an empty plan = the kit is complete (delivered in step {advisor_step}; re-rendered by lybra sync after master changes)
step5.title_local: Advisor readiness check ({label} session directory advisor kit steady state)
step5.check_local: onboarding check outputs '✓ Step {step} prerequisites satisfied'; sync --dry-run outputs 'up-to-date: 0 file(s) to fetch/render'
step5.pull_head: # Fetch the charter at session start (run first every time a {label} session opens at {session_at}; the output = the full rendered advisor charter, including the keep-moving rules):
step5.land_head: # Fetch the charter and skills at session start (run first in the session directory every time a {label} session opens at {session_at}; the session writes them itself, the product never pushes):
step5.title_remote: Advisor readiness check ({label} session: prerequisite self-check + fetch the charter at session start)
step5.check_remote: onboarding check outputs '✓ Step {step} prerequisites satisfied'; no .pi/ under the governance root, no advisor kit added on this machine
step5.purpose: The new advisor ({label} session at {session_at}) confirms the products of steps 1–{advisor_step} are complete: the governance root {gov}/.lybra/ has its own advisor credential and role (owner_policy_ref = project grant {auth}), and the advisor kit is in place (local session) or is fetched at session start (remote session)
step5.fail_advisor_key: Step {advisor_step} not done / no advisor credential in the governance root
step5.fail_advisor: Ask the Owner to rerun step {advisor_step} (--dry-run first, then --confirm)
step5.fail_grant_key: Step {grant_step} not done / no project grant
step5.fail_grant: Ask the Owner to run step {grant_step} to sign the project grant, then run step {advisor_step}
step5.fail_plan: Run lybra sync --harness-root <governance root> once without --dry-run and check again; still not empty = report a bug with the --dry-run --json output
step5.fail_foreign_key: the charter landing already holds a non-Lybra file
step5.fail_foreign: The session directory already has a file of the same name (not rendered by Lybra): move it away or use another session directory, then rerun lybra sync (user files are never overwritten)

enroll.fail_no_role_cred: Step {advisor_step} not done (no advisor credential in the governance root); ask the Owner to run step {advisor_step} first
enroll.fail_unknown_root: The gate cannot find the project; make sure the gate and step {project_step} use the same home root
enroll.fail_envelope: The step {grant_step} project grant is not signed or does not cover this instance (the instance host segment must be among the grant's hosts); check lybra project grant show {pq} --home-root {hq} (pre-check refusal = no code issued)
enroll.fail_401: The gate rejected the advisor credential or the code (issuing gate ≠ this gate); check connection.json mcp.rpc_url and rerun this step (on failure the code is already revoked)
enroll.fail_rollback: When enrollment fails the gate has already revoked the code (output shows it was rolled back); if the rollback failed, revoke by hand per the exit in the output and rerun
enroll.fail_ambiguous: The command already carries --project {pq} (the gate's explicit target project, AIPOS-F282); if PROJECT_AMBIGUOUS still appears, check that --project is a project registered under the home root and is the same project as --governance-root

station.title: Enroll{sep}{label} (pi, {mode} mode): {instance} @ {ws}
station.comment: # {label}: preview with --dry-run first (role / instance / governance root / landing / covering grant, no code issued, zero writes), then --confirm; the enrollment code stays inside this process; the credential lands in the workstation .lybra + .pi wiring (owner_policy_ref derived from project grant {auth})
station.purpose: {duty}. The advisor uses its own credential (governance root .lybra/connection.json, projects=[{project}]) to issue and redeem the code on the governance-root machine in one command; workstation directory {ws} (source: {ws_source}); one directory is enrolled for one instance only
station.check: --dry-run outputs a preview and the covering grant; --confirm outputs the executed line, code_id and fingerprint (never the code itself) and 'role (with owner_policy_ref)'; the workstation .lybra/connection.json has lybra_bin and workspace_root == governance_root
station.fail_pi: Enrollment lands the .pi wiring and the step {sync_step} sync adds any declared mount that is missing; still missing = report a bug (attach the sync --json output)
station.fail_bin: Enrollment writes the running lybra deployment location; rerun this step with the deployed lybra command
station.fail_root_key: workspace_root written as the harness root
station.fail_root: workspace_root must equal the governance root inside the code; rerun this step to correct it
station.creates: {ws}/.lybra + .pi + AGENTS.md; land event of the enrollment in the governance root (workstation={ws})
station.duty_audit: Audits always go to the independent pi auditor workstation {instance} (it never audits its own cards)
station.duty_exec: Every non-code card (docs / governance / config / validation) is done by the pi executor workstation {instance} (loop launches pi per the grant, or the Owner runs /go at the workstation)

step8.title: Enroll the sub-agent executor ({mode} mode, spawned by the {kind} advisor session): {instance} @ governance root
step8.comment: # Sub-agent executor: the credential lands in the governance root .lybra/connection.json (per-instance entry), harness = the advisor session {kind}; no workstation, no sync, no pi (for code cards the advisor spawns a sub-agent from the lybra kickoff brief, which delivers under this identity)
step8.purpose: The execution identity for code cards {instance} (instance host segment = the advisor session's machine): credential and governance seat both land in the governance root {gov}; the land event records mode={mode} harness={kind} (no workstation= part = no workstation location, pi cannot be dispatched to it); different name and directory from the pi executor workstation {pi_instance}
step8.check: --dry-run outputs a preview; --confirm outputs the executed line and the land event (mode=subagent); no new .pi/ under the governance root
step8.fail_harness: Sub-agent mode needs --harness <advisor session kind> (here = {kind}) and no --harness-dir; rerun this step's command as is
step8.fail_target: In sub-agent mode the credential must land in the governance root: --workspace must be {gov}
step8.creates: {gov}/.lybra/connection.json sub-agent executor entry + land event (mode={mode}, harness={kind})

step9.declare: # Declare the execution division (AIPOS-F143 / F256, enforced by card type): code cards = sub-agent executor, every non-code card = pi executor workstation, audits = independent pi auditor workstation; draft defaults and the publish identity check read this declaration (preview first, then write and land)
step9.review: # Review: all three instances enrolled (✓) and the execution division section shows the pi executor workstation
step9.title: Declare the execution division (project set-execution, all three) and review
step9.purpose: Declare once who executes what in this project: code cards → sub-agent executor {code}; non-code cards → pi executor workstation {noncode}; audits → pi auditor workstation {audit}. Identities are checked before writing (each must be an instance enrolled in this project; the auditor and the pi executor must have a workstation location)
step9.check: set-execution --dry-run gives the project.json diff (zero writes), --confirm writes and lands it ('verdict=PASS'); roles list shows all three instances ✓ and the execution division line names the pi executor workstation instance
step9.fail_missing_key: instance not enrolled / no workstation location
step9.fail_missing: Go back to steps {first}–{last} to enroll the instance, then rerun this step
step9.fail_same: The auditor must be an independent pi auditor workstation instance, never equal to any executor

step10.station: # {label} workstation: land the workstation kit per the distribution declaration → steady-state check → workstation self-check (read-only, names each missing item)
step10.plan: # Workstation setup status (read-only; the three instances' enrollment, workstation charter freshness and the execution division)
step10.title: Workstation sync + steady-state check + workstation self-check
step10.purpose: The pi executor workstation {exec_ws} and the auditor workstation {audit_ws} get skills / extensions / charter per the distribution declaration; check the steady state and self-check the minimum bootable set (the sub-agent executor has no workstation and is not synced); workstations only sync, they never run gate verbs
step10.check: sync reports the workstation lines as synced (the first workstation also gets .pi/extensions/go.ts); --dry-run outputs 'up-to-date: 0 file(s) to fetch/render' and no would-prune lines; onboarding check outputs '✓ Step {step} prerequisites satisfied'; workstation-plan shows all three instances enrolled and fresh workstation charters
step10.fail_skipped_key: sync marks the workstation as skipped
step10.fail_skipped: --workspace-root must be this project's governance root {gov}
step10.fail_plan_key: the --dry-run plan or prune is not empty
step10.fail_plan: Run sync once without --dry-run and check again; still not empty = report a bug with the --dry-run --json output
step10.fail_not_enrolled: That workstation is not enrolled: go back to step {audit_step} / {exec_step} and enroll-deliver it
step10.fail_selfcheck: Fix each missing item in the output (dangling lybra_bin → rerun the matching enrollment step; owner_policy_ref missing → check that the step {grant_step} grant covers this workstation, then rerun sync)
step10.creates: workstation kits of {exec_ws}, {audit_ws}; workstation parent root _distributed/

step11.publish: # Publish the card: the card draft JSON gives project / task_mode / lane.repo (a step 2 repo name) / audit etc. (executor / harness / auditor default from the step 9 execution division); validated, then published to pending
step11.drive: # Drive: lybra loop finds project grant {auth} by itself (no envelope), claims in one go (builds the worktree) → waits for the return → dispatches the audit → waits for the audit report → verdict → finalize → close → N6 landing
step11.code: # Code card: when loop asks for a sub-agent, the advisor takes the self-contained kickoff brief and spawns a sub-agent in the advisor session (as {instance}) that follows it; the sub-agent stops once RETURN is written
step11.noncode: # Non-code card (and audit card): loop launches pi at the pi executor / auditor workstation per the grant; when the grant does not allow launching, the Owner starts it by hand at that workstation (same for the auditor workstation, cd {audit_ws}):
step11.title: First card: publish → lybra loop drives it to close (code card = sub-agent / non-code card = pi executor workstation)
step11.purpose: The advisor drives only with product commands: lybra loop drives the whole card under project grant {auth}; execution follows the step {execution_step} division: for a code card the advisor spawns a sub-agent with lybra kickoff, for a non-code card loop launches pi at the pi executor workstation {exec_ws} (or the Owner runs /go there); audits are done by the pi auditor workstation {audit_ws}. Executors / auditors only write products (RETURN / audit report); every gate action is done by the product
step11.check: lybra loop exits 0 and outputs 'done: <card ID> …' with the closure record present and governance landed (after closing, loop runs the N6 landing itself: lybra governance-commit --task-id)
step11.fail_5: The step {grant_step} grant is not signed or does not cover this card (lane / task mode / host); ask the Owner to sign the widening command from the output
step11.fail_3: The executor / auditor has not returned its product yet: for a code card make sure the sub-agent was spawned, for a non-code card make sure pi was launched or /go was run, then rerun the same lybra loop
step11.fail_status_key: check progress (loop runs in the background / silent for long)
step11.fail_status: lybra loop status --task-id {task} --workspace-root {gov} (reads the run record + liveness + stall check: running/stalled/launch_dead/loop_dead/ended, with log paths); never judge by tail/grep of raw logs
step11.fail_gate: Handle it per the output as is; loop has read back the gate records and will not repeat steps already done
step11.fail_landing: N6 landing refused (someone else's staged files / guard / push not done): handle it per the output, then rerun the same lybra loop (landing is idempotent)
step11.fail_go_key: /go says the worktree is not built yet
step11.fail_go: Claiming and building the worktree are done by the driver, workstations never claim themselves; wait for lybra loop to claim, then /go
step11.creates: The card in the completed queue + claim/return/dispatch/verdict/finalization/closure records, committed and pushed to the governance repo

summary.head: Full flow to onboard new project {project} ({count} steps, zero manual editing; Owner one-time actions = Step {owner_steps}):

gate_start.title: Get the gate running (signing grants / codes and loop all talk to the gate from here on)
gate_start.foreground_note: keep the terminal open, closing it stops the gate; good for a first try
gate_start.resident_note: Linux = systemd --user unit, macOS = launchd; preview the full unit text first, then --confirm (enables it and reads the state back); uninstall with `lybra serve uninstall --confirm`
gate_start.check: The gate item of lybra setup check is ✓ (probing {gate})
gate_start.skip: The pre-flight check shows the gate already running and reachable; this step can be skipped

card_policy.comment: # Card ID pattern (task_id_pattern, AIPOS-F252): card ownership resolution for controlled release / finalize / lybra-deploy reads only this, and the product has no built-in default; show suggests a value from existing card ID prefixes (a suggestion only); once the Owner confirms the value, preview first and then --confirm (writes card_policy.json in the governance root and lands it)

legacy.meta: # The project.json description keys ({keys}) are updated through the product write entry as well (no hand-editing of old manual-era text); preview first, then --confirm
legacy.meta_none: # The project.json description key write entry lybra project set-meta becomes available once config.schema project_json declares those keys (undeclared = refused with META_KEY_UNDECLARED)
legacy.t1: Landing declarations: declare project.json paths through the product write entry (no hand-editing)
legacy.c1_head: # Keys and values are validated against config.schema project_json.paths (unknown keys refused / finalize_mode enum); preview the diff with --dry-run first, then --confirm
legacy.c1_stage: # If the stage archive (stage snapshots) is not in the default place, declare it the same way: --key {key} --value <path relative to the governance root> (undeclared = default location; no snapshot there = the finalize stage gate refuses)
legacy.p1: Why first: the next two steps work from the declared locations: freezing finds cards by queue_root, adoption writes report skeletons by return_root and loop finds products by the declarations; undeclared locations take defaults, and a manual-era project's real locations are not necessarily the defaults, so skeletons would land in the wrong place. Declare the manual-era project's Return / verdict / queue / authorization locations one by one (several --key/--value pairs allowed; declare explicitly even when equal to the default: adoption requires config.schema project_json.paths.adoption.required_declared_keys to be declared explicitly, otherwise it refuses with ADOPT_PATHS_UNDECLARED). If the stage archive (stage snapshots) is not in the default place, also declare {key} (relative to the governance root): the stage gate of Lybra's internal finalize checks stage snapshots at that location, and undeclared with no snapshot at the default location = refused (AIPOS-F145). The first preview line names the target project and the absolute project.json path; --confirm once it checks out; inside the target project's governance root the project name can be omitted (target = that root's project.json#project; unresolvable = refused, never falling back to the home-level active project; an explicit project name that differs from the governance root you are in = refused)
legacy.t2: Freeze the backlog: declare manual-era cards that are finished / no longer driven as history in one go (migration baseline)
legacy.c2_head: # Check the cards to be frozen and each card's lint problem count with --dry-run first, then switch to --confirm (the list is append-only; unfreeze = --unfreeze)
legacy.p2: Why before adoption: adoption honors freezing (a frozen card is refused with ADOPT_LEGACY_FROZEN), so first declare the cards no longer driven as history in one go and leave the cards still in flight that should continue out with --exclude (for the next step to adopt); frozen cards are not reported as ERROR by state lint, not treated as pending by next, and the gate refuses write actions on them
legacy.t3: Adopt in-flight cards: the gate back-fills the claim record, binds the existing branch and builds the card worktree
legacy.c3_head: # For each in-flight card: preview first (zero writes, with the authorization judgment and every refusal), then --confirm once there are no refusals; after adoption drive it with lybra loop like a new card
legacy.p3: Why last: adoption writes report skeletons and claim records and depends on the previous two steps (locations declared, history cards frozen). --branch = the existing branch holding the card's products (in the card's lane.repo); when the card branch name differs, the card branch is created on its tip. Refusals (declared in transitions nodes.N1.adoption.guards + config.schema project_json.paths.adoption.guards) are listed all at once: missing required card intent / branch not found / gate-issued claim already present / frozen / locations undeclared / card branch diverged / worktree creation failed / grant not covering. An existing hand-written Return is never overwritten: loop asks for commit_sha / tree_hash / branch per the return criteria, and the refusal says how to add them
